Appendix: Analyses Explanation

Design and coding. Early Odds = participants saw the DraftKings American odds before making predictions (data label “American Odds Condition”); Late Odds = odds were shown after predictions (“No Odds Condition”). Participants predicted which team would advance, then allocated up to 100 tokens across the matches; tokens kept above 100 earned 1 cent each. In each match the favorite is the team with the lower American odds; USA vs. Belgium (-110/-110) has no favorite and USA is treated as the favorite. Sportsbook probabilities are implied probabilities with the vig removed (each team’s implied probability divided by the two teams’ sum).

Table 1 (matchups). Odds and which team advanced in each match; teams are ordered as in the paper.

Participant information and demographics. Median and IQR of completion time, percentage receiving a bonus, and mean bonus among recipients; counts and percentages for each demographic category. “Other” race/ethnicity combines American Indian/Alaska Native, Middle Eastern/North African, South Asian, and other responses.

Probability by odds condition. For each match, a Welch t-test compares Early and Late Odds probabilities for the first-listed team. The two teams’ probabilities sum to 1, so one test per match suffices and the underdog’s mean is 1 minus the favorite’s with an identical SD. p-values are Holm-corrected across the 12 matches; d is the pooled-SD standardized difference.

Affinity. Five-point ratings (1 = strongly negative, 5 = strongly positive) of each team; stacked bars show the percent choosing each option, with M (SD) at right.

Bets. “% Bet on” uses the Block 3 bet choice; “Mean tokens” uses the final bet with 0 tokens recorded for the team not bet on.

Expected value (EV). For each team, EV per 100 tokens computed from the participant’s own stated probability and the odds shown: EV = p x (100 + profit) - 100, where profit = 100 x 100/|odds| for negative odds and equals the odds for positive odds. Believed advancer = team given the higher stated probability; higher-EV team = team with larger EV. A match is discordant when these are different teams. Odds-condition differences in discordance and in choosing the believed advancer within discordant matches use logistic regressions with participant-clustered standard errors (Early vs. Late odds ratio, Wald z).

Brier scores. A participant’s Brier score is the mean over matches of the squared difference between the probability assigned to a team and the outcome (1 if it advanced, 0 otherwise). Mean individual Brier score within a match equals (mean probability - outcome)^2 + variance of probabilities across participants, which the tables call collective error (the group as a whole is wrong) and dispersion (participants disagree with one another). This decomposition is exact, needs no probability bins, and does not depend on which team is labeled the event. Confidence intervals come from a cluster bootstrap (2,000 resamples of participants, keeping each participant’s matches together). Early vs. Late differences in mean Brier score use Welch t-tests (d = pooled-SD standardized difference). Reference strategies: always 50/50; always back the favorite with certainty (0.5 for the no-favorite match); the sportsbook de-vigged probability. Correlations are Pearson correlations of participants’ mean Brier score with final tokens and number of bets won.

Normalized HHI. The Herfindahl-Hirschman index of the share of wagered tokens across matches, rescaled to run from 0 (even spread across all k matches) to 1 (all tokens on one match): (HHI - 1/k)/(1 - 1/k). Participants who wagered no tokens are excluded. The strategy value is the normalized HHI of putting half the tokens on one match and spreading the rest evenly: (.25 + .25/(k - 1) - 1/k)/(1 - 1/k), k = 8 (R16) or 4 (QF).

Bet amount groups. Within each sample, bettors were split 80/20 (seeded) into training and testing sets. Normalized HHI and the proportion of matches bet on were standardized with training moments; k-means (50-100 random starts) was run for k = 2 to 6 and k = 3 chosen from variance explained and average silhouette width. Groups are ordered by HHI: Spreaders, Selectors, Concentrators. A depth-3 decision tree fitted to the training clusters gives threshold rules that are applied to the testing set (percent reproducing the k-means assignment) and then to all bettors, so group membership can be reproduced without clustering. Stability is the mean Jaccard similarity of each training cluster across 200 bootstrap re-clusterings. Group differences in % of matches correctly predicted, final tokens, and mean Brier score use one-way ANOVAs (partial eta-squared) and, where significant, Games-Howell post hoc tests (Tukey-Kramer-type p with unequal variances; d with pooled SD).

New Analysis 1 (bets on the favorite). The outcome is whether the Block 3 bet was on the favorite (1) or the underdog (0), for each participant x match (USA is treated as the favorite against Belgium). The correlation table includes the outcome as the first variable (point-biserial correlations) followed by the probability assigned to the favorite, affinity for the favorite, affinity for the underdog, affinity difference (favorite - underdog), EV of betting on the favorite and on the underdog and their difference, and the payoff SD of each bet and their difference. Only the lower triangle is shown; asterisks mark correlations significant after Holm correction across all pairs, using participant-clustered standard errors (each correlation is the slope of a regression of one z-scored variable on the other). The descriptives table gives the mean (SD) of the same variables (except the outcome) separately for bets on the favorite and bets on the underdog. The payoff SD for a 100-token bet is (profit + 100) x sqrt(p(1 - p)), because the bet returns the profit with probability p and loses 100 otherwise. (The plain Bernoulli SD sqrt(p(1 - p)) is identical for the two teams, so it could not be entered separately for each.) Three logistic regressions are fitted in each sample, with predictors standardized within sample (odds ratios per 1 SD): Model 1, the probability assigned to the favorite; Model 2, EV and payoff SD of the favorite and of the underdog; Model 3, the EV difference and the payoff SD difference. Because the models have different predictors, each is presented in its own table with the Round of 16 and Quarterfinals samples side by side. VIFs are reported for Models 2 and 3. Within a match, EV and SD are exact functions of the probability assigned to the favorite, so the EV and SD terms are identified only by differences in odds across matches, and matches are pooled. All standard errors are clustered on participant.

New Analysis 2 (affinity). Correlations are between the affinity difference (favorite - underdog) and (a) the probability difference (p favorite - p underdog) and (b) the difference in final tokens (favorite - underdog). Reported as pooled Pearson, within-match Pearson (match means removed), and pooled Spearman (ranks). Each is a standardized regression slope with participant-clustered 95% CIs. A second table restricts to matches with unequal affinity and tests whether the higher-affinity team was picked or bet on more than 50% of the time (intercept-only logistic regression, clustered). A third table estimates the affinity-difference effect after controlling for the probability assigned to the favorite. The last table gives each participant’s Spearman correlation between a team’s affinity and tokens wagered on it across all teams seen, with a t-test on Fisher-z values.

New Analysis 3 (anchoring). USA vs. Belgium is excluded. Deviation = participant’s probability for the favorite - de-vigged sportsbook probability for the favorite. Condition differences (Early minus Late) in absolute and signed deviation are linear regressions with match fixed effects; binary outcomes (estimate within 2 points of the sportsbook; picked the favorite; bet on the favorite) are logistic regressions with match fixed effects; all use participant-clustered standard errors. The figure shows the empirical cumulative distribution of the signed (top row) and absolute (bottom row) deviation, in percentage points, for Early and Late Odds in each sample (columns); large grid lines mark every 10 points and small grid lines every 5. A curve that sits to the left (absolute deviation) means estimates were closer to the sportsbook probability.
